samples.summary: Default start affinity for plain (non-cell) selections silently flipped backward→forward, changing rendering for five out-of-diff consumers of `computeSelectionRects`
samples.evidence: Before this change the non-cell branch of `buildRects` called `positionToPagePixel`/`findPageForPosition` with no affinity, i.e. the `'backward'` default (pagination.ts:385). It now uses `start.lineAffinity ?? 'forward'` (selection.ts:260), and the in-code comment claims this "keeps the historical reading" — true only for the cell-internal branch. Every caller that passes ranges with no `lineAffinity` gets new behaviour at wrap boundaries: peer selections (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1620), search highlights (editor.ts:1640-1643, endpoints are bare `{blockId, offset}`), comment markers (editor.ts:1659-1660, anchors come from `pathToDocPosition` which never sets affinity — packages/frontend/src/app/docs/comments/decorations.ts:24), spell-error squiggles (editor.ts:1676-1680), and text-box selections (packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:560). A highlight whose start offset lands exactly on a wrap boundary now begins on the following visual line instead of the closing one, and the single-line vs multi-line branch (`startPixel.y === endPixel.y`) can flip with it. None of these consumers was updated or covered by the new test.

samples.summary: Peer caret rendering still hardcodes 'backward' while the peer's selection now honours per-endpoint affinity, so a peer's caret and the edge of their highlight can land on different visual lines
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1561-1566 calls `resolvePositionPixel(peer.position, 'backward', ...)`, ignoring `PeerCursor.position.lineAffinity` (the field is now part of `DocPosition`, packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:210). Meanwhile peer selections go through `computeSelectionRects` (editor.ts:1620) which now reads `anchor.lineAffinity`/`focus.lineAffinity`. At a wrap boundary the peer caret paints at the end of line N while their selection edge paints at the start of line N+1.

samples.summary: `DocsPresence.activeCursorPos` type was not extended with `lineAffinity` even though `updateCursorPos` now publishes it at runtime
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:2999 publishes `clampedPos`, which `clampPosToModel` (line 964-968) now copies `lineAffinity` onto, into `activeCursorPos`. But `packages/frontend/src/types/users.ts:21-24` still declares `activeCursorPos?: { blockId; offset }`, so every reader (docs-view.tsx:226 building `PeerCursor.position`, docs-detail.tsx:56) type-erases the field and the caret half of the feature is dropped for peers. Only `activeSelection` was widened.

samples.summary: `restoreLocalCursor` drops the newly propagated `lineAffinity` when re-seating the local caret after a remote change, while it keeps it on the restored selection
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3592-3600: `cursor.moveTo({ blockId, offset })` is called without the second `affinity` argument, so `Cursor.lineAffinity` resets to `'backward'` (packages/docs/src/view/cursor.ts:13,30), even though `resolveAnchoredDocPosition` now returns `lineAffinity` (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:1072) and `selection.setRange(range ?? null)` on the next line preserves the endpoint affinity. After any remote edit the caret and the selection edge disagree at a wrap boundary.

samples.summary: `anchorDocPosition`'s default changed from `'backward'` to `undefined`, changing what unrelated call sites store and what `resolveAnchoredDocPosition` now hands back
samples.evidence: The parameter default was removed (yorkie-doc-store.ts:918) and `setCompositionStart` (line 1204) now calls it with no affinity at all, so `compositionStartAnchor.lineAffinity` becomes `undefined` where it was `'backward'`. Combined with the new echo-back at lines 1054/1072/1124, `resolveAnchoredLocalCursor()` now returns `DocPosition`s carrying (or missing) affinity that downstream consumers — `editor.restoreLocalCursor`, `editor.updateCompositionStartPosition` (docs-view.tsx:368-373) — were written against the old, affinity-free shape. `undefined` at a start endpoint is not equivalent to `'backward'` any more, because `buildRects` now defaults a missing start affinity to `'forward'` (selection.ts:260).

samples.summary: Presence design doc still documents the old `activeCursorPos`/`activeSelection` shapes without `lineAffinity`
samples.evidence: docs/design/docs/docs-presence.md:88-95 declares the presence payload as `{ blockId, offset }` for both cursor and selection endpoints, and line 271 repeats `activeCursorPos { blockId, offset }`. The runtime shape changed in packages/frontend/src/types/users.ts:29-30 and yorkie-doc-store.ts:2999. This file lives under docs/design/<topic>/ so the top-level ref check does not cover it.

finding.summary: Default start affinity for plain (non-cell) selections silently flipped backward→forward, changing rendering for five out-of-diff consumers of `computeSelectionRects`
finding.evidence: Before this change the non-cell branch of `buildRects` called `positionToPagePixel`/`findPageForPosition` with no affinity, i.e. the `'backward'` default (pagination.ts:385). It now uses `start.lineAffinity ?? 'forward'` (selection.ts:260), and the in-code comment claims this "keeps the historical reading" — true only for the cell-internal branch. Every caller that passes ranges with no `lineAffinity` gets new behaviour at wrap boundaries: peer selections (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:1620), search highlights (editor.ts:1640-1643, endpoints are bare `{blockId, offset}`), comment markers (editor.ts:1659-1660, anchors come from `pathToDocPosition` which never sets affinity — packages/frontend/src/app/docs/comments/decorations.ts:24), spell-error squiggles (editor.ts:1676-1680), and text-box selections (packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:560). A highlight whose start offset lands exactly on a wrap boundary now begins on the following visual line instead of the closing one, and the single-line vs multi-line branch (`startPixel.y === endPixel.y`) can flip with it. None of these consumers was updated or covered by the new test.

verdict.reason: The factual core is accurate — selection.ts:260 now defaults a non-cell start endpoint to 'forward' where the old path defaulted to 'backward' (pagination.ts:385, selection.ts:190), and all five/six cited consumers do pass bare {blockId, offset} endpoints (editor.ts:1620, 1640-1643, 1659-1660, 1676-1680, 3129; text-box-editor.ts:560). But the impact does not reach the lens's major bar of 'a caller left broken or inconsistent'. Tracing positionToPagePixel (selection.ts:200-233) and the multi-line branch (selection.ts:486-535) for the exact scenario claimed (start offset on a wrap boundary): under the old 'backward' default startPixel.x equals getLineEndX(line0) (selection.ts:503), so the first rect has width 0, the interior-line loop (selection.ts:516) emits nothing, and the last rect (selection.ts:528-534) spans getLineStartX(line1) → endPixel.x — the same geometry the new single-rect 'forward' path produces. The new behaviour therefore differs only by dropping an invisible zero-width rect (a zero-width rect also cannot hit-test in commentMarkerRects or getSpellErrorAt), plus a one-line-height shift of rects[0].y in the scroll-into-view at editor.ts:3137 toward the line the match actually occupies. The test file itself documents the old output as 'a zero-width tail on line 0 plus all of line 1' (selection-line-affinity.test.ts:110-114), and the affinity-less default IS covered by the new test (selection-line-affinity.test.ts:117-125, exercising the non-cell branch since blockParentMap is empty at test:53), contradicting the 'not covered by the new test' part of the claim. This is at most a minor consumer inconsistency plus an inaccurate 'historical reading' comment — real, but non-blocking under this rubric.
